column1: # Where to get out-of-tree PostgreSQL extensions, and what they need.
# THIS FILE DOES NOT DECIDE VERSIONS. Which plugins a run includes, and at which
# version, is a per-workspace decision -- it is the experiment variable, and
# comparing pgaudit 16.1 against 17.1, or a plugin before and after a fix, is
# exactly what workspaces are for. The `ref` column here is only a default for
# when a workspace does not say.
# What IS global, because it is a property of the plugin rather than of any
# experiment: where it lives, what it needs to build, whether it must be
# preloaded, and what name CREATE EXTENSION wants.
#     plugins=pgaudit                 registry repo, registry default ref
#     plugins=pgaudit@17.1            registry repo, THIS workspace's version
#     plugins=x@https://git/x.git@v2  no registry involvement
#     plugins=x@/path/to/tree         a working tree on this host
# Refs are verified by scripts/plugins-verify.sh, not trusted: tag conventions
# are inconsistent (v3.0 vs v3.0.0, VERSION_4_16_3 vs 4.16.3, REL2_3_1 vs
# 2.3.1), so a version number does not tell you the tag. Two of the seventeen
# defaults below were wrong when first written, and the verifier is what caught
# them.
# pgfuzz fetches each into ~/.cache/pgfuzz/plugins/<name> on the HOST, copies it
# into the source export at plugins/<name>, and build.sh builds it with PGXS
# against the tree being built. Nothing is fetched inside the build container,
# so a build stays reproducible and works without network.
# Everything here is pinned for PostgreSQL 17.10.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   name      extension name, and the CREATE EXTENSION name unless `create` says otherwise
#   version   the release being pinned
#   repo      git URL
#   ref       tag or branch to check out
#   apt       build dependencies to install in the image (space-separated, or -)
#   preload   yes if it must be in shared_preload_libraries, else no
#   create    the SQL name to CREATE EXTENSION, or - to skip (library-only)
#   notes     why it may not build, or what it needs
# WHAT WILL NOT BUILD, AND WHY -- stated up front rather than discovered at 3am:
#   mysql_fdw    needs BOTH libmariadb-dev and libmariadb-dev-compat. The first
#                installs headers under /usr/include/mariadb/; mysql_fdw.h does
#                a plain #include <mysql.h>, so without the -compat package that
#                provides the /usr/include/mysql/ path the build dies with
#                "mysql.h: No such file or directory" after everything else has
#                already built. Found 2026-08-24, on the first build that asked
#                for the whole catalogue at once.
#   oracle_fdw   needs Oracle Instant Client, which is proprietary and cannot be
#                downloaded unauthenticated. Listed, marked, and skipped unless
#                ORACLE_HOME is provided. Everything else here is open source.
#   postgis      builds, but pulls a large dependency chain (geos, proj, gdal,
#                protobuf-c, json-c). Slow first build; fine afterwards.
#   timescaledb  requires cmake and its own build step; the .so is large.
#   citus        likewise heavy, and wants a specific PG major -- 13.2 targets 17.
#   postgis, timescaledb -- and anything else using cmake or autogen/configure
#                rather than plain PGXS -- currently FAIL THE BUILD, on purpose.
#                The instrumented second pass only knows how to rebuild a PGXS
#                plugin (clean, then CC/CXX/COPT so the sanitizer flags survive
#                Makefile.global); the cmake/configure branch falls back to the
#                uninstrumented first-pass artifact. Shipping that would mean an
#                extension that loads, runs, reports coverage and detects
#                nothing -- so the instrumentation check stops the build instead.
#                Teaching those two build systems to take the sanitizer flags is
#                what unblocks them; until then a workspace cannot request them.
# preload=yes matters: those libraries do their work from _PG_init() under
# process_shared_preload_libraries_in_progress, and CREATE EXTENSION fails
# outright without it. pgfuzz adds them to shared_preload_libraries
# automatically; that is what the `preload=` workspace knob feeds.
